look_here_first: This is a SMALLER-HEADED Paspalum complex: first spot one to a few fine one-sided flowering racemes, sometimes with axillary heads. The excellent existing macro shows tightly fitted pale green spikelets and PURPLE dangling flowering anthers/stigmas. Check actual leaf hair arrangement, raceme number and mature glumes; P. setaceum includes several varieties that a single seedhead photo cannot resolve.

crew_field_steps: Examine one raceme close up: green flattened spikelets alternate along the axis; purple flower parts project from several.
Differentiate purple protruding anthers/stigmas from seed awns; the seedhead is not a foxtail or purple flowering plume.
Before naming a variety or separating from P. pubiflorum/distichum, obtain leaf blade/hairiness, ligule, whole plant and mature measured spikelets.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Complete plant showing basal or cauline leaf development and hair density.
Terminal vs axillary one/few flowering racemes in the same frame.
Flowering macro showing the pale spikelet and protruding purple anther separately.
Mature measured spikelet with upper glume pubescence plus sheath/ligule close-up.

comparisons.key_distinctions: P. setaceum often has one to few narrow racemes with relatively small spikelets and highly variable varieties differing in blade hairiness. Creeping wet-ground P. distichum typically has two terminal racemes and obvious stolons, while P. pubiflorum often has several racemes and larger spikelets. A single closeup of spikelets is not enough to prove variety.
